# SchoolOS — Onboarding Run Log: building a real school, end to end, through the UI only

> **What this document is.** A complete, replayable record of onboarding a real school
> into SchoolOS the way a person does it — only by clicking in the browser. Every click,
> every keystroke, every HTTP request and response, every screenshot, every console error.
> The machine-readable transcripts are in [`docs/onboard-raw/`](onboard-raw/) and the
> screenshots are in [`shots/onboard/`](../shots/onboard/).
>
> **Companion document.** Every defect, gap and improvement this run uncovered — with root
> cause, file:line, severity and the fix that was applied — is in
> **[`ONBOARDING-FIXES.md`](ONBOARDING-FIXES.md)**.

Two things about these numbers, stated plainly rather than smoothed over.

**The 8 transferred pupils are an artefact of re-running flows, not a school policy.** Several
flows were executed more than once while I was chasing defects, and each run enrolled its
children afresh. Six names — Advait Rao, Diya Kulkarni, Ishaan Nair, Myra Sheikh, Reyansh
Bhat, Saanvi Joshi — therefore appear twice: once active, once transferred by the later
run's withdrawal step. A real school would not look like this; it is the residue of an
iterative onboarding run, and it is why the audit log has 397 entries for a school of 28
pupils.

**One payment was taken and then fully refunded**, so it is counted in receipts and not in
collected money — the round trip is the point, and `RCP-000001` is in `app.fee_receipts`.

The audit, event and action counts are those read at the end of the flow sequence; the bulk
import in flow 20 added a handful more afterwards.

## 2. How this was driven, and why the numbers look the way they do

A real Chrome (Puppeteer, headless, 1440×1000) loaded the real Vite dev server, which
served the real React app, which called the real Fastify API, which wrote to the real
Postgres. Nothing was stubbed, mocked or seeded behind the app's back. The instrumentation
captured, for every single step:

* the action taken (navigate, click, type, choose) and a full PNG of the screen;
* a dump of **every** `<input>` / `<select>` / `<textarea>` on the page with its label,
  type, value, required and disabled flags — this is the proof of what was actually typed,
  because React controlled inputs are easy to fool by inspection;
* every request: method, URL, request headers (auth redacted), **request body**;
* every response: status, response headers, **response body**;
* every `console.error` and uncaught exception;
* every native dialog (`window.confirm` / `window.prompt`), which the harness answers on
  the user's behalf — the app raises a `window.prompt` for the step-up password when a
  403 `stepUpRequired` comes back.

**Three mechanical artefacts inflate the counts, and they are all real findings:**

1. **Every API call has a CORS preflight.** `liveApi.ts` sets
   `content-type: application/json` on *every* request, including bodyless `GET`s. A
   `content-type` is a non-safelisted header, so even a `GET` becomes a preflighted
   request. This **doubles** the request count against the API. The driver records the
   preflights explicitly; the per-step tables below list only the real call.
2. **Every effect runs twice.** React StrictMode double-invokes effects in development, so
   each screen issues its data fetch twice on mount.
3. **A cold page load always produces a `401 POST /auth/renew`.** See finding **C-1** —
   the browser never received the session cookie, so session restore cannot work.

## 3. Backend reachability through the frontend — the short answer

The question this run was built to answer is *"is the backend actually available through
the frontend?"* The honest, measured answer:

| Verdict | Domains |
|---|---|
| **Fully working end to end through the UI** | school signup · classes/sections · subjects · staff accounts · first-sign-in password change · student enrolment · student **edit (PATCH)** · student withdrawal · class assignment · attendance marking · library catalogue · loan policy · issue · return · circulation report · fee heads/plans · fee generation · fee ledger · **payment → confirm → receipt → refund** · fee policy save · concessions with maker-checker · admissions funnel (capture → stage lattice → activity) · timetable seeding · **teacher homework** · **teacher lessons** · **teacher leave** · announcements · board pack + snapshot · certificates · **custom role create/edit/assign** · **approval delegation** · **bulk roster import from CSV (with a per-row report)** · **timetable period + slot authoring** · audit · work orders · visitors · plugins |
| **Backend exists and is correct, the UI just does not call it** | `/today` (should call `GET /actions`) · `/operations` (should call `GET /work-orders`, `GET /assets`) · `/cases` (should call `GET /cases`) · `/memory` (should call `GET /memory`) · `/learning` exam creation (no create form at all) · teacher copilot/curriculum/mastery/analytics/progress-story (client marked "PROPOSED") |
| **Reachable, but one field short** | A timetable slot stores `teacher_name` as free text with `teacher_id: null`, so the substitution engine cannot match a teacher who is ill (**P2-15**). `POST /timetable/clash-check` has no button (**P2-16**). |
| **Deliberately correct that they look wrong** | A Principal composing an announcement is offered **Approve**, and the server refuses it — segregation of duties. The button should be hidden, not the rule (**P2-10**). |
| **Blocked by a missing UI, backend ready** | register ownership before any teacher can mark attendance (**fixed here** — F-1) · 12 of 29 plugins could not be switched on (**fixed here** — C-2) · create a **student account** (no entry point at all — G-1) · link a **parent** to a child (the form has only Full name / Email / Role — G-2) · create an **exam** (no form — G-3) · **retire a custom role** (the client declares the DELETE and never calls it — G-6) · **list or revoke an API key** (no caller anywhere — G-7) |
| **Screen is sample/placeholder data, honestly labelled** | `/reception`, `/data-health`, `/documents`, `/automation`, `/constitution`, `/ai-governance`, `/ai-usage`, `/group`, `/it` |
| **Not buildable through the UI at all** | the whole `/student/*` portal (no way to create a student account) |

Every claim above is backed by a step in Part 2 of this document.

## 4. What a brand-new school can and cannot do on day one

Measured by visiting all **121 routes** as each of five roles, recording the API calls each
screen makes, the visible text it renders, and whether it refuses the caller:

| Role | Screens visited | Refused | Screens with a 5xx | Screens rendering sample data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | 121 | 42 | 0 | 21 |
| Librarian | 121 | 102 | 0 | 1 |
| Teacher | 121 | 72 | 0 | 8 |
| Finance head | 121 | 83 | 0 | 10 |
| Coordinator | 121 | 59 | 0 | 12 |

Zero 5xx responses after the library fix (**F-6**). The refusals are correct — a teacher
cannot open the fee ledger, a finance head cannot open the library desk. The sample-data
column is the one that matters: those screens *say* they are illustrative, which is honest,
but on several of them a live door already exists and simply is not called.

## 5. The ten defects that stopped the onboarding, in the order they were hit

Each is fixed in place; the full analysis, diffs and severity table are in
[`ONBOARDING-FIXES.md`](ONBOARDING-FIXES.md).

| # | Severity | One line |
|---|---|---|
| **C-1** | P0 | `@fastify/cors` v11 defaults `methods` to `GET,HEAD,POST` — so **every** `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` door in the API failed its browser preflight. `PUT /school/classes` — the single most important onboarding step — was impossible from a browser. |
| **C-2** | P0 | The Add-ons board was driven by a hand-maintained client registry of 19 plugin ids while the server registers 29. **12 plugins could never be switched on from the UI**, including `teacher.classroom`, `exams.assessment`, `student.world` and `parent.assistant` — and the kernel treated a server-enabled plugin as OFF if the client had never heard of it. |
| **F-1** | P0 | Nothing in the SPA ever called `GET`/`POST /class-assignments`. Because `POST /attendance/mark` is gated on a teacher owning the register, **no teacher could ever mark attendance**. |
| **F-2** | P0 | `GET /plugins/library/members` did `ORDER BY s.grade::int` on a **free-text** grade column → `invalid input syntax for type integer: "Grade 8"` → **HTTP 500**. The borrower picker was empty, so no book could be issued to anybody. |
| **F-3** | P0 | "Reset password" read `r.tempPassword` while the server returned only `temporaryPassword`, so the mint modal rendered an **empty** one-time password — the account was left holding a hash nobody had the plaintext for. Unrecoverable lockout. |
| **F-4** | P1 | The attendance register did `Number(grade)`. A school that names its grades "Grade 1"…"Grade 8" (exactly what the Classes screen tells you to do) got a picker reading **"Grade NaN-A"** and an **empty register**. |
| **F-5** | P1 | A school Finance head was shown a **disabled** "New plan" button captioned *"Fee plans are managed by finance, the principal or the owner — your role can view them."* The server allows `finance_head` and `finance_clerk`. Only the owner could build a fee structure. |
| **F-6** | P1 | The library members picker listed **withdrawn** pupils as borrowable; the issue door then refused them with a 409 that named nothing about which row was wrong. |
| **F-7** | P1 | Leaving the *optional* "Quiet hours" field blank on the library policy screen sent `[0]` and failed the **entire save** — none of the other 20 settings persisted. |
| **F-8** | P1 | "Start from the standard day" was offered to a coordinator and returned `403 role coordinator not permitted`: the button was gated on the write list, the door on the retire list. |
| **F-13** | P1 | Three teacher screens (`MasteryMap`, `ClassAnalytics`, `CurriculumProgress`) hard-code `useState('8')` for the grade, so a teacher who owns Grades 1–5 is shown **Grade 8** data — and coverage saved via `POST /curriculum/progress` is written against the wrong class. The server already returns the teacher's own classes in `scope.classes` and `ownedClasses()` already exists. |

Also found and fixed: the fee-plan grade scope was hard-coded `1..10` instead of the school's
own classes (**F-12**), the borrower picker offered withdrawn pupils (**F-6**), and the
optional "Quiet hours" field failed the whole library policy save (**F-7**).

And found but **not** fixed, because they are decisions rather than patches: the browser
never receives a session cookie, so a refresh always signs you out (**C-3**).
